opportunities.title: They Blamed 'Bad Actors.' The Bad Actor Was the Business Model.
opportunities.why_now: A Trump-linked account promoted GOLD before it collapsed, and the entity now denies launching it while pointing at 'bad actors' — a script this channel has seen a hundred times.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition breakdown: annotate the promote-crash-deny timeline with a checklist readers can reuse next time a 'trusted' account shills a token

opportunities.title: Your Ledger Is Only as Safe as Your Last Update: The Replacement Attack Nobody Patched
opportunities.why_now: OneKey just reproduced a transaction-replacement exploit on an outdated Ledger Ethereum app, proving 'cold storage' isn't a security state, it's a maintenance schedule.
opportunities.angle: Technical explainer + firmware-check callout, framed as 'the hack that only works because you didn't update' — evergreen security PSA with a fresh proof-of-concept hook

opportunities.title: Cosmos Labs Cleared the Bug. The Bug Then Caused a $5.7M Six-Chain Hack.
opportunities.why_now: Cosmos Labs admitted it wrongly signed off on the exact bug that later enabled a six-chain exploit, exposing how little 'audited' actually guarantees.
opportunities.angle: Audit-theater takedown: use this as Exhibit A in a running series on why security reviews fail, ending with a rule of thumb for evaluating 'audited' claims

opportunities.title: One Wallet, 10% of Supply: How Fogo's Mainnet Got Halted by a Single Exploit
opportunities.why_now: An attacker received 400 million FOGO — a tenth of circulating supply — forcing the L1 to halt mainnet, a governance/security failure at a scale that demands a postmortem before the official one drops.
opportunities.angle: Fast-turn incident breakdown with a supply-concentration risk lens: what a 10% mint/transfer to one address says about validator/permission design

opportunities.title: The Card Was the Attack Surface: How a $1.1M Exploit Crashed a Neobank's Token 49%
opportunities.why_now: A live drain on a Solana neobank's card contract (Avici/Rain) tanked the token 49% in real time, showing how 'crypto debit card' products quietly reintroduce custodial attack surfaces.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive on crypto-card architecture risk — tie together the Avici exploit and the CoinDesk neobank piece as one trend, warn readers evaluating card products
